entries.answer:
The build prompt is ready as a Markdown document. It converts the full blueprint — planning-first core, wide-research orchestration, validation loop, persistent sandbox memory, tool framework, domain pipelines, provenance, tiers, and safety controls — into 13 sequential build steps.[1]

## What the prompt covers

- **Hard constraints (Step 1–2):** exactly one backend file (Python/FastAPI/SQLite) and one `index.html` containing all subpages; an explicit ban on placeholders, mocks, stubs, and fake logic; no mention of the original product's name anywhere.
- **Architecture (Steps 3–7):** the nine components with their responsibilities and interactions, the full data model (event stream, plans, DAG steps, artifacts, provenance, checkpoints, secrets, tier policies), the beam-search-style candidate planning algorithm with scoring and replanning triggers, the parallel sub-agent roles (scout, summarizer, verifier, synthesizer) with dedup and weighted-vote conflict resolution, and all four validation primitives with their correction triggers.
- **Execution and delivery (Steps 8–13):** the tool adapter pipeline with concrete tools (sandboxed shell, code execution, spreadsheet engine, headless browser with success detection and human-approval routing), the spreadsheet/code-mobile/design pipelines, provenance metadata, the three-tier cost/latency routing, secrets redaction and PII scrubbing, the complete REST + SSE API with an explicit state machine, and all eight frontend views.
- **Acceptance bar (Step 13):** concrete verifiable tests — resume-from-checkpoint, cost-cap halting, secret-leak checks, and a runbook with launch commands.

One deviation I deliberately made from a literal reading of the source: the blueprint references third-party services (e.g., a mobile preview toolchain, chat/automation integrations); I generalized these into implementable requirements (QR-code dev-server preview, approval-gated browser flows) so the prompt stays buildable without naming external products.
